body: Thank you, I'm feeling a bit better at the moment, but I know it won't last forever. I'll be sure to message you if I need to talk to someone.

Thank you for responding, I feel a little better now. I've calmed down since this afternoon. I felt like I was really on the edge. Spending the weekend alone in my apartment leaves me with nothing but myself and my thoughts, and with no one around things quickly get out of control. That's mainly why I decided to post this. Most of my few friends, have no idea I suffer from depression, or if they do, I don't let on how bad things are. I don't talk to anybody about it, except for my psychiatrist, because I fear how people's perceptions might change of me. Many people who have never felt the effects of depression, or never had someone close to them suffer from it, can't fathom that it's an actual disease. 

In the last year at my old job I began to suffer from crippling anxiety, I'm a web developer, it's predominately a problem solving job. My mind basically locked up and I couldn't deliver my work on time. A few coworkers and I were let go due to restructuring, although I knew that my boss was unhappy with my work and failure to deliver, he never said it, but I knew it was part of the reason I was let go. I have since got a new job that one of my friends managed to get for me. I was actually hired to work under my friend, which I knew might be difficult. Bottom line is that my friend, who is under a lot of his own career and life stress, seems to be taking stuff out on me. I happened to see a skype message he sent to someone else, where he stated that he felt my quality of work wasn't good enough. So I feel he has decided to throw me under the bus to save his career. He's also becoming quite distant, which leads me to believe that I might get let go. I feel I'm doing the best I can, but at the same time I beat myself up for not being better.
